raw_transcript:
Okay, so, recording this on the train home, it's, uh, Thursday the 8th of October. Long day. So the main thing today was the Cedar Metrics ingest service, the Go one, and the, um, the duplicate events problem that Ivo Penn flagged last week. Ivo's the on-call lead this rotation. So the symptom is that the events table in PostgreSQL gets duplicate rows when the Kafka consumer rebalances. And we, we kind of assumed it was the consumer committing offsets too late, which, okay, it partly is. What I actually did today: I wrote a reproduction. I spun up a local Kafka with three partitions, no, wait, it was six partitions, I changed it after lunch because three didn't trigger it, and I forced a rebalance every 90 seconds. Over a 40 minute run I got 212 duplicate rows. So that's reproducible now, which honestly is the best news of the week.

Then I paired with Nella Voss, she's the staff engineer on the data platform team, and she suggested, instead of fighting the offset timing, just make the insert idempotent. So we added a unique constraint on event_id plus source and switched the insert to ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. Ran the same 40 minute repro and got zero duplicates. Zero. But, and this is important, that is local only. I did not merge it. The PR is open, it's PR 1184, and it needs a review from someone on the DBA side because adding a unique index on a table that size is not, um, not trivial. The events table is about 310 million rows. Nella thinks building the index concurrently will take maybe 2 hours, but nobody has actually tested that on a production-sized copy, so that's a guess.

Oh, and side note, the coffee machine on four is broken again, so I had the, the tea from the kitchen which was, let's just say, not great. Anyway.

Latency. I also measured insert latency because Ivo was worried the conflict check would slow things down. p99 went from 18 milliseconds to 21 milliseconds in the local run. Sorry, let me correct that, it was p95, not p99. p95 went from 18 to 21 milliseconds. I didn't look at p99 at all, actually, I should do that tomorrow. So it's a 3 millisecond hit on p95 in a local setup, which, I mean, probably fine, but I don't want to claim that's what production will see.

What else. The rollout plan. Ivo wants it behind a feature flag, the flag is going to be called ingest_idempotent_insert, and we roll it out to the staging cluster first. That's planned for Monday, um, the 12th. I have not created the flag yet. Then if staging looks okay for 48 hours, we go to production. The deadline from Priya Okafor, our engineering manager, is October 23rd, because the analytics team has a quarterly report that depends on clean counts.

One thing I'm not sure about is whether the duplicates we already have in production need a backfill cleanup. I think, I think yes, there's maybe a few hundred thousand duplicate rows, but I don't have a real number, I just eyeballed one day of data. I'll ask Nella if her team has a dedup script. I did not write any cleanup script today.

Also I filed a ticket, CM-447, for the offset commit thing anyway, because even with idempotent inserts we're doing extra work on every rebalance. That's not fixed, that's just a ticket.

Okay, to-dos for tomorrow: check p99, ask the DBA channel about the concurrent index build, create the feature flag, and write up the repro steps in the PR description so Ivo can run it himself. That's it. Train's at my stop.

Oh, one more thing I forgot. In standup Priya asked whether we could also, um, use this chance to add a dead letter topic for events that fail schema validation, because right now those just get logged and dropped. I said yes, but, like, not in this PR. Separate ticket. I don't think anyone wrote that ticket. I'll write it. Also Ivo mentioned the consumer group has 8 instances in production, so the rebalance storm on deploy is way worse than my local six partitions, which, honestly, explains a lot. I haven't confirmed how often prod actually rebalances, he just said "a lot", which is not a number.
